title: Put a table fan back together after washing: blade onto the shaft's pin, reverse-thread cap, front grille, three clips
context: Table fans gather dust, and makers tell owners to take the grille and blade off to clean them (Midea FT30-8MB manual: "Plastic parts should be cleaned with mild soap and damp cloth or sponge", "Dry all parts completely before reassembling"). Putting one back is four fits, each easy to get wrong. The Comfort Zone CZ121 manual: "Place fan blade onto motor shaft. Notice the pin on motor shaft should fit into slots of fan blade." "Thread blade cap onto threaded end of motor shaft. Note: Threads are reversed at this connection. Tighten=Counter-clockwise." "Be sure the front grille is inserted into rear grille support on the bottom of rear grille." "Press the three (3) grille clips on rear grille to securely attach to front grille." A switched-off motor's shaft turns freely, so the blade has to be stopped while the cap is turned (a third maker has the cap unscrewed "while holding the metal shaft tightly"). The instruction says none of this.
setup: Cm from the midpoint between the arm bases, x away from the robot, y to its left. Sizes are estimates for a 12 inch fan. (1) Table fan, unplugged, fixed in place, lying on its back on a folded towel (46 x 30 x 2.5 cm), motor shaft up, base away from the robot: white plastic housing; rear grille on it, rim 34.9 cm across with its top 11.2 cm above the towel, a support at its far side (a hook 4 cm wide whose lip reaches 5 mm in, 4 mm above a seated rim) and three sprung clips on its left, right and near sides, standing open; steel shaft 8 mm thick ending 15 cm above the towel in an 8 mm long thread, a 3 x 16 mm cross pin 12.5 cm up. The shaft turns freely. (2) Blade, 70 g, blue plastic: three blades, 30 cm across, on a hub 4.4 cm across with an 8.6 mm bore and a slot 4.6 mm wide and 7 mm deep across its back. It lies on a folded tea towel (20 x 20 x 2 cm). (3) Blade cap, 10 g: an eight-sided plastic knob 3.8 cm across and 1.8 cm tall, on the table. (4) Front grille, 110 g, white plastic: rim 34.9 cm across and 1 cm thick, ribs domed 7.6 cm high to a round badge. It lies on a dish rack (a 30 x 30 x 14 cm block). Layout A: shaft at (24, -10), pin along x; blade (44, -42); cap (22, -43); grille (55, 20), turned 30 degrees from the way it goes on. Layout B: shaft (25, -9), pin turned 15 degrees; blade (45, -41), turned 15 degrees; cap (19, -44); grille (56, 20.5), turned 25 degrees. Both arms start raised in the ready pose.
scoring: Scored at the end; the highest row that holds. 0.25: the blade is on the shaft with the pin at the bottom of the slot in its hub (hub within 1.5 mm of the shaft's axis and 3 degrees of square, its back face within 1 mm of its seat; riding on top of the pin it stands 7 mm high and does not count). 0.5: also the cap is on the thread and tight (turned anticlockwise until the thread draws its face against the hub's, within 0.8 mm). 0.75: also the front grille lies on the rear grille's rim (centred within 3 mm, no point of its rim more than 2 mm up, turned within 6 degrees) with its bottom edge under the support's lip. 1.0: also all three clips are shut over its rim (within 6 degrees of fully in), both grippers are at least 3 cm from every part, and everything is at rest (in the last half second no part or clip has moved more than 2 mm or turned more than 3 degrees). 0 otherwise, whatever else was done.
reset_notes: Open the three clips, lift the front grille off, unscrew the cap (clockwise), lift the blade off, put the three parts back on their marks, and turn the shaft so that its pin points as the layout says.
fidelity: Rigid colliding shapes: shaft, pin, hub bore and slot, cap bore, rims, support lip, clips. Sizes are estimates, not measured. The thread is not cut: once the cap's bore is 2.5 mm over the shaft's end a joint keeps it on the axis and draws it down 4 mm a turn (coarser than real), with thread friction that carries the free shaft round. Clips are hinges with over-centre springs. Blades are flat plates. The fan body is fixed; no cord. Let go, the shaft may creep (under 2 degrees a second).
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (both arms drew back to their bases; later the right gripper hovered over the fan's shaft; no part was picked up); demo: 1.0
